title: JavaScript Mastery Test
description: Test your core JavaScript expertise: closures, prototypes, event loop, promises, ES6+, and DOM APIs.

questions.question: What is a Closure in JavaScript?
options: A function bundled together with references to its lexical environment, allowing it to access outer variables even after the outer function has executed
A method that terminates an infinite while loop
A keyword used to close a database connection
An HTML tag that closes a script tag
questions.explanation: Closures allow an inner function to retain access to variables declared in its enclosing lexical scope even when invoked outside that scope.

questions.question: What is the output of `console.log(0.1 + 0.2 === 0.3)` in standard JavaScript?
options: false
true
undefined
NaN
questions.explanation: Due to IEEE 754 floating-point binary representation, `0.1 + 0.2` equals `0.30000000000000004`, which is strictly not equal to `0.3`.

questions.question: What is the difference between `==` and `===` in JavaScript?
options: `==` performs type coercion before comparison; `===` checks both value and type strictly without coercion
`===` converts both operands to strings
`==` can only compare numbers
There is no difference in modern ES6+
questions.explanation: Strict equality `===` evaluates to true only if both operands are of the same type and hold the same value.

questions.question: What is 'Hoisting' in JavaScript?
options: Variable and function declarations are moved to the top of their containing scope during compilation before code execution
Lifting elements up in the DOM tree
Compressing JavaScript code into smaller files
Assigning values to undefined variables automatically
questions.explanation: Hoisting allocates memory for variable (`var`) and function declarations during the creation phase of the execution context.

questions.question: What is the 'Temporal Dead Zone' (TDZ) regarding `let` and `const` variables?
options: The period between entering the scope and the actual line where the variable is declared, during which accessing it throws a ReferenceError
The time taken for a Promise to time out
The interval between setTimeout calls
The delay when loading scripts with async or defer
questions.explanation: Unlike `var` which initializes as `undefined`, `let` and `const` remain uninitialized in the TDZ until their declaration line is executed.

questions.question: What does `Promise.all([p1, p2, p3])` do if one of the promises rejects?
options: It rejects immediately with the error of the first rejected promise, ignoring other pending promises (fail-fast)
It waits for all promises and returns both errors and successes
It retries the failed promise up to 3 times
It silently replaces the rejected promise with null
questions.explanation: Promise.all is all-or-nothing: if any input promise rejects, the entire returned promise rejects immediately.

questions.question: How does the `this` keyword behave inside an Arrow Function compared to a regular function?
options: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they retain the `this` value of the enclosing lexical scope
Arrow functions always bind `this` to the global `window` object
Arrow functions create a dynamic new `this` context on every invocation
Arrow functions throw an error if `this` is used inside them
questions.explanation: Arrow functions establish `this` based on the scope in which the arrow function was defined (lexical scoping).

questions.question: What is the purpose of `Array.prototype.reduce()`?
options: Executes a reducer callback function on each element of the array, resulting in a single accumulated output value
Removes all duplicate items from an array
Shortens the array length by half
Sorts the array in descending order
questions.explanation: `.reduce()` iteratively aggregates array values into a single accumulator result (e.g. sum, grouped object, flattened array).

questions.question: What is Event Bubbling in the browser DOM?
options: An event triggers on the deepest target element first and then propagates upwards through its parent ancestors in the DOM tree
Events propagate downward from the window to the target element
Events are executed in parallel across Web Workers
Events that trigger animated bubbles on screen
questions.explanation: During event bubbling, an event triggers on the inner target element first, bubbling up through each parent element unless `event.stopPropagation()` is called.

questions.question: What is the difference between `deepCopy` and `shallowCopy` of an object containing nested objects?
options: A shallow copy only duplicates top-level properties (nested objects share references); a deep copy duplicates all nested objects recursively
Shallow copy converts objects to arrays
Deep copy only works on primitive types
Deep copy deletes the original object
questions.explanation: Shallow copying (`Object.assign` or spread `{...obj}`) keeps nested object references pointing to original memory, whereas deep copies (e.g. `structuredClone()`) clone all nested levels.
